trajectory.title: Trajectory
trajectory.content: Digital services and connectivity businesses are experiencing steady multi-year growth driven by robust subscriber additions, increased customer utilization, ARPU growth, and scale-up of digital services [1, 3, 5]. In the retail sector, grocery digital orders and overall digital revenues are demonstrating strong growth with increasing order values and customer bases [4, 5]. Conversely, retail EBITDA margins have compressed due to the increased growth of digital revenues [4].

balance_sheet.title: Balance sheet
balance_sheet.content: For the standalone entity, the debt-equity ratio increased to 0.41 in 2025-26 from 0.37 in 2024-25 [5]. Total standalone non-current borrowings were 22,789 crore and current borrowings were 31,392 crore as of 31st March, 2026 [3]. The company's net working capital is negative [1], with a standalone current ratio of 0.99 for 2025-26 [5].

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.content:
1. Capex is starting to taper down as the bulk of the capex, including 5G and UBR core network deployment, is mostly complete across the country [1]. 
2. Management maintains its directional target of doubling absolute EBITDA practically in two years, moving from the year of consolidation to high-growth years [3, 8]. 
3. Management guided to continuing the expansion of the dark store network and going deeper into markets over the next 9 to 12 months [5]. 
4. Management has not set a specific margin target, focusing instead on growing absolute EBITDA and driving operating leverage through scale [8].

bull: Operating revenues increased 11.4% year-on-year to Rs. 40,475 Crores, and EBITDA grew 16.6% year-on-year to Rs. 21,879 Crores [4].
JPL operating revenues grew 12% with EBITDA growing faster due to operating leverage, achieving an EBITDA margin of 53.3% [7].
The quick commerce business is positive at the contribution margin level [5].
bear: Margins have come down with the scaling up of the quick commerce business and online businesses, leading to a consistent lower margin trajectory [2].
Depreciation and finance costs increased due to a higher asset base and higher debt, reflecting in a higher profit after tax decline of 24% against an EBITDA decline of 10% to 11% [2].
